document.description: Lawful Permanent Resident status in the United States grants visa-free or simplified entry privileges to multiple international jurisdictions.

unlocks.conditions: Lawful permanent resident of the United States holding a valid Green Card and valid passport from country of citizenship
unlocks.navigation_path: Home > Immigration and citizenship > Visit Canada > Entry requirements
unlocks.official_quote: As a lawful permanent resident of the United States you don't need a visa or eTA to travel to Canada. When travelling to Canada, you must travel with your United States green card and a valid passport from your country of citizenship.
unlocks.exactQuote: As a lawful permanent resident of the United States you don't need a visa or eTA to travel to Canada. When travelling to Canada, you must travel with your United States green card and a valid passport from your country of citizenship.

unlocks.notes: US permanent residents are exempt from the eTA and visa requirements to travel to Canada.

unlocks.conditions: Permanent resident of the United States (Green Card holder) + valid passport
unlocks.navigation_path: Inicio > Visas para extranjeros > Visa Exemptions
unlocks.official_quote: United States citizens and foreigners who are permanent residents (green card holders) or with a valid visa stamped on their passports, do not require a visa to travel to Mexico on tourism or non paid activities and stay up to 180 days.
unlocks.exactQuote: United States citizens and foreigners who are permanent residents (green card holders) or with a valid visa stamped on their passports, do not require a visa to travel to Mexico on tourism or non paid activities and stay up to 180 days.
